title: Mathematicians say OpenAI doesn't understand its own Navier-Stokes proof
excerpt:
OpenAI submitted a 166-page solution to the Navier-Stokes problem but apparently doesn't fully understand its own proof. Several groups of experts dispute the claimed methodology, saying the actual approach differs from what OpenAI described. And because language models are black boxes, where the underlying ideas came from will likely never be clear.
The article Mathematicians say OpenAI doesn't understand its own Navier-Stokes proof appeared first on The Decoder .

ai.summary: OpenAI released a 166‑page manuscript claiming a solution to the Navier‑Stokes existence and smoothness problem, but multiple mathematicians say the methodology described does not match the actual work and that the model likely cannot explain its own reasoning.
ai.why: It highlights limits of current language models for generating reliable, verifiable mathematical proofs, warning developers against treating AI‑generated research as authoritative.

title: Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes
excerpt:
Anthropic's AI model Claude has solved a 25-year-old cryptography puzzle. The mysterious seeds behind NIST's standard curves for digital signatures were provided by the NSA without explanation, raising long-standing suspicion about built-in backdoors. Claude figured out in under 30 minutes that the seeds came from "lrand48," a simple C random number generator, making deliberate backdoors far less likely.
The article Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes appeared first on The Decoder .

ai.summary: Anthropic’s Claude determined that the seed values for NIST’s elliptic‑curve digital‑signature standards were generated with the C library function lrand48, resolving a 25‑year‑old suspicion of NSA‑inserted backdoors.
ai.why: Shows large language models can aid cryptographic analysis and may influence future standards reviews.
